::: {.main-message}
Near places are alike. So places are not independent observations, and our methods need to account for that.
:::

## Load


::: {.cell caption='Run me first (spdep takes a moment)'}
```{webr}
#| caption: "Run me first (spdep takes a moment)"
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(spdep)

data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maczokni/crime_mapping_workshop/main/data/"
lsoa <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "lsoa.csv")) |> st_as_sf(wkt = "geometry", crs = 27700)

vehicle <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "crimes.csv")) |>
  filter(crime_type == "Vehicle crime") |>
  count(lsoa21cd, name = "vehicle")

d <- lsoa |>
  left_join(vehicle, by = "lsoa21cd") |>
  mutate(vehicle = coalesce(vehicle, 0L))
```
:::


## Spot the real map

- One map is real. Three are the same values **shuffled at random**.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
#| fig-height: 6
set.seed(2024)
real <- sample(1:4, 1)

game <- bind_rows(lapply(1:4, function(i) {
  values <- if (i == real) d$vehicle else sample(d$vehicle)
  d |> mutate(map = paste("Map", LETTERS[i]), value = values)
}))

ggplot(game) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = value)) +
  facet_wrap(~ map) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  theme_void()
```
:::


Guess first, then check:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
LETTERS[real]
```
:::


## 1. Neighbours

- Queen contiguity: neighbours share any boundary point.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
nb <- poly2nb(d, queen = TRUE)
summary(nb)

links <- nb2lines(nb, coords = st_centroid(st_geometry(d)), as_sf = TRUE)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = d, fill = "grey95") +
  geom_sf(data = links, colour = "#5b2a86") +
  theme_void()
```
:::


## 2. Spatial lag

- Spatial lag: the average of each area's neighbours.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
w <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W")   # weights sum to 1 for each area
d$lag <- lag.listw(w, d$vehicle)

d$vehicle[1]          # area 1
d$vehicle[nb[[1]]]    # its neighbours
d$lag[1]              # their average
```
:::


## 3. Moran's I


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
d <- d |> mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(vehicle)), z_lag = lag.listw(w, z))

ggplot(d, aes(z, z_lag)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Vehicle crime (standardised)", y = "Neighbours' average") +
  theme_minimal()
```
:::


- Slope = Moran's I. Test: 999 random shuffles, as in the game.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
set.seed(1)
moran.mc(d$vehicle, w, nsim = 999)
```
:::


## Your turn

Is every crime type clustered? Try `"Burglary"`, `"Shoplifting"`, `"Anti-social behaviour"`.


::: {.cell setup='true' exercise='ex_moran'}
```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: ex_moran
library(sf); library(dplyr); library(spdep)
data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maczokni/crime_mapping_workshop/main/data/"
lsoa <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "lsoa.csv")) |> st_as_sf(wkt = "geometry", crs = 27700)
w <- nb2listw(poly2nb(lsoa), style = "W")
```
:::



::: {.cell exercise='ex_moran'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_moran
counts <- read.csv(paste0(data_url, "crimes.csv")) |>
  filter(crime_type == "______") |>
  count(lsoa21cd)

x <- lsoa |> left_join(counts, by = "lsoa21cd") |> mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0L))
moran.mc(x$n, w, nsim = 999)
```
:::


::: {.hint exercise="ex_moran"}
Exact spelling, e.g. `"Burglary"`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex_moran"}
- Anti-social behaviour: I ≈ 0.28, clustered.
- Burglary: I ≈ 0.10, p ≈ 0.08. **Not** significant. 67 areas and one month give weak evidence.
- Shoplifting: I ≈ 0.06. Shops are scattered islands.
:::

## 4. Where? Local Moran's I (LISA)

- One test per area (67 tests), adjusted for multiple comparisons.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
set.seed(1)
lisa <- localmoran_perm(d$vehicle, w, nsim = 499, alternative = "two.sided")

d$p <- p.adjust(lisa[, 5], method = "fdr")
d$cluster <- ifelse(d$p < 0.05, as.character(attr(lisa, "quadr")$mean), "Not significant")
table(d$cluster)

ggplot(d) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cluster)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("High-High" = "#d7191c", "Low-Low" = "#2c7bb6",
                               "High-Low" = "#fdae61", "Low-High" = "#abd9e9",
                               "Not significant" = "grey92")) +
  theme_void()
```
:::


::: {.callout-important}
## Think
If you ran a regression on these 67 areas, which of its assumptions would this break?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## From GIS?
- GeoDa: *Univariate Moran's I* / *Local Moran's I*
- ArcGIS: *Spatial Autocorrelation* / *Cluster and Outlier Analysis*
- In R: weights, permutations, seed and correction are all in the script. Fully reproducible.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Know R?
- Rook weights: `poly2nb(d, queen = FALSE)`. Or k-nearest: `knn2nb(knearneigh(st_centroid(st_geometry(d)), k = 5))`. Does I change?
- Rates vs counts: join `population.csv`, test vehicle crime per 1,000 residents.
- Regression residuals: `lm.morantest(lm(vehicle ~ 1, d), w)`. Then `spatialreg::lagsarlm()`.
- Tidy interface: [`sfdep`](https://sfdep.josiahparry.com/).
:::
